We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}) & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=7{x}^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int 7{x}^{2}\,dx=\frac{7{x}^{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}7{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})(\frac{7{x}^{3}}{3}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}(\frac{7{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\frac{7({e}^{3})^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(({e}^{3})^{2})}{3}-\frac{7(1)^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡((1)^{2})}{3}]-\frac{14}{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{7{e}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{6})}{3}-\frac{14{x}^{3}}{9}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}} \\  & =14{e}^{9}-(\frac{14{e}^{9}}{9}-\frac{14}{9}) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(126{e}^{9}-14{e}^{9}+14) \\  & =\frac{14}{9}(8{e}^{9}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
